rgb: The camera wearer is positioned on an upper concrete ledge looking downward into a narrow, unfinished concrete-walled shaft framed in the distance by a stepped red-brick wall on the right and a vertical red-brick pillar on the left, both out of reach at roughly 3 to 5 metres away. Directly in front of and below the camera wearer on the mortar ledge at about 3 to 5 metres rests an orange-handled trowel out of reach, while a concrete stairway lies about 2 to 3 metres to the left of the brick pillar in the first frame and a horizontal white pipe spans the shaft walls about 2 to 2.5 metres ahead and below. Deeper inside the shaft, roughly 0.5 to 1.5 metres below the camera wearer and about 3 to 5 metres below the white pipe, a person stands between the narrow walls holding an item 3 to 5 metres away and out of their own reach while tilting their head downward to face and look directly away from the camera wearer. Across the five frames from right to left, the camera wearer leans and moves backward by roughly 0.5 to 0.8 metres while angling the viewpoint further downward into the opening between the brick walls, causing the left-side stairwell to pass out of view after the first frame. As the camera retreats away from the ledge across the sequence, the distant brick structures and trowel shift toward the bottom and side borders of the frame and become partly cut off, while the person below transitions from being mostly occluded by the narrow opening and shadow in the first two frames to being clearly visible above the knees in the final three frames.
depth: The depth map captures the steep vertical geometry of an unfinished masonry shaft, rendering the distant jagged brick ledges and columns dark grey-black (~3–5 m from the camera wearer, out of arm's reach) and the approaching plastered side walls as smooth gradients brightening toward white at the shaft floor (~0.5–1.5 m below, within arm's reach). Across frames 1 to 5, as the wearer moves leftward and leans away from the opening, the brick column shifts from the centre-left (~3–5 m) to the extreme left edge (~3–5 m) while the stepped brick wall on the right moves into the distant lower-right background (~3–5 m), exposing the shallow central drop between them. Compared to the dimly lit RGB strip, the depth map makes it much easier to read the continuous 3D slant of the side walls, the stepped depth of individual protruding bricks, and the recessed depth of the horizontal white pipe (~2.5 m down) spanning the shaft above the nearby person. However, the map is unreliable for small distant objects and dark recesses: the trowel and level resting on the ledge out of arm's reach (~3–5 m) are smoothed into the ledge surface, and the person standing ~0.5–1.5 m below (facing and looking downward away from the wearer) is swallowed by the black background in frames 1–4 before appearing only as a faint grey blob in frame 5.
segmentation: In frame 3, the segmentation map isolates a brown 'person' mask for the worker standing ~0.5–1.5 m below at the bottom of the shaft between the side walls, who is facing and looking downward away from the camera wearer while holding a small object 3–5 m away and out of their own arm's reach. Aside from that single detection, the map fails to track the worker in frames 1–2 (where they are in shadow and partly occluded by the distant ledge) and frames 4–5 (where they shift slightly right relative to the frame as the wearer peers away from the edge). While the frame 3 mask helps separate the nearby worker's silhouette from the dark shaft background where RGB contrast is low, the segmentation map is overwhelmingly unreliable across the sequence. It completely misses the trowel and level out of the wearer's arm's reach (~3–5 m on the lower ledge) and hallucinates false labels onto the surrounding masonry: misclassifying the walls and brick pillar in frame 1 as gigantic 'person' and 'tie' masks, the right-side stepped bricks (~3–5 m) and left brick pillar (~3–5 m) in frame 2 as 'carrot' and 'person', the left-edge bricks (~3–5 m) in frame 3 as 'person', and the bottom-right bricks (~3–5 m) in frame 4 as 'teddy bear'.
pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. From the RGB strip, the camera wearer's hands and body remain out of the field of view behind the camera (with a trowel and level resting out of arm's reach at ~3–5 m on the distant ledge in frames 1–3), while another person stands ~0.5–1.5 m below at the base of the narrow shaft, ~3–5 m below the horizontal white pipe. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer shifts leftward and tilts downward away from the gap between the right and left brick walls, this nearby person passes from partial occlusion behind the distant ledge in frames 1–2 into clear overhead view in frames 3–5, facing and looking down away from the wearer with their arms angled backward holding an item 3–5 m away and out of their reach. Because the pose estimator outputs nothing at all, it adds no spatial clarity over the RGB frames and is completely unreliable under this steep top-down viewing angle, ~0.5–1.5 m distance within reach, and dim shaft lighting.
